subject: Nebula Labs — request for bespoke latency and availability guarantees
messages:
From: Sam Tan <sam.tan@nebulalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Renewals <renewals@nebulalabs.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Nebula renewal — bespoke uptime & latency asks

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the renewal discussion earlier. Nebula's procurement team has circled back with a tighter set of asks for our upcoming multi-year renewal: they want a written commitment to a 99.995% monthly uptime (SLA) plus a P95 inference latency of <= 80ms for their production traffic using our hosted endpoint for embeddings and chat.

They've highlighted three conditions that make this request firm:
- Core workload is low-latency inference on shorter sequences (average 120 tokens) at ~120 reqs/s peak.
- They are willing to move to a dedicated pool / reserved capacity and accept a meaningful price uplift.
- They require a runbook and an operational escalation path with 24/7 on-call and monthly latency reports.

Attached is their formal RFP (SLA_RFP_Nebula.pdf) and a short note from Renewals. Can you and the product/infra leads confirm whether this is feasible and what the cost implications are? Need our internal answer by EOD next Wednesday as they target a Sept 22 signature.

Best,
Sam

--
Sam Tan
Head of Platform Partnerships, Nebula Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Nebula renewal — bespoke uptime & latency asks

Looping you in. Nebula is strategic (Exp. ARR: $3.2M/year) and pushing for a written availability/latency pledge as part of renewal. They explicitly said they'd accept dedicated capacity and a price uplift, but want the SLA bound to our hosted API endpoint (not self-hosted).

Quick asks:
- Karthik: what data on expected token throughput and model variants do you need to assess feasibility?
- Vivek: rough risk estimate & what operational controls we'd need to put in place (canaries, pre-warm, cache policies).
- Ava: can we get legal/finance sign-off window for an exception if infra signs off?

I've attached Nebula's RFP.

Marissa
Sales, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SLA_RFP_Nebula.pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Nebula renewal — bespoke uptime & latency asks

Thanks for the context — initial technical notes below.

Short answer: technically possible but only under a constrained deployment pattern and with operational changes. Key items we need confirmed from Nebula before committing:
1) Traffic distribution: sustained qps vs short spikes, and percent of requests that are streaming vs single-shot.
2) Model family and max sequence — you mentioned embeddings + chat; which specific models/weights are they using? Small quantized LLMs behave differently under KV cache pressure.
3) Tolerance for occasional model-fallbacks and an agreement on max allowed fallbacks per month.

Operational / infra asks to hit 99.995% + P95<=80ms:
- Dedicated GPU pool pinned to their account (reserved nodes) with auto-burst policy disabled except for documented emergency procedures.
- Continuous batching disabled for their low-latency tier; instead we use per-request routing to low-latency execution path. This increases cost per token.
- Prefix/KV cache warming and a pre-warm policy during expected traffic windows.
- Active synthetic canaries and 1-min granularity latency dashboards + alerting to on-call.

Estimate: 30–45% cost uplift versus standard hosted, depending on committed tokens and model choice. If they accept a dedicated pool and price uplift, we can hit the p95 target for the short sequences mentioned.

I can draft a short technical rider to attach to the SLA if we confirm the workload shape.

-Karthik
Senior Product Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Nebula renewal — bespoke uptime & latency asks

Appreciate the detail, Marissa / Karthik. Operational risk summary and suggested approval path:

Risk summary:
- Dedicated pool reduces noisy-neighbor blast radius but adds capacity-management burden and costs.
- P95 <= 80ms is achievable in steady-state for short sequences but vulnerable to large-fanout spikes and model fallback events.
- Our current SRE SLOs and alert runbooks need a small extension for the 99.995% target (we currently guarantee 99.9% for hosted in public docs).

Suggested mitigation package to offer Nebula (conditional approval):
1) Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) + 30–40% price uplift.
2) Operational runbook (attached: operational_runbook_draft.md) including:
   - 24/7 on-call escalation, runbook steps, and RTO/RPO expectations
   - Canary plan and roll-back triggers
   - Monthly latency and availability reporting cadence
3) Canary + staging mirrored traffic for 30 days before go-live.
4) SLA language: include carve-outs for force majeure, planned maintenance windows, and documented model-fallback exceptions.
5) Executive pre-approval for a one-time mitigation credit (up to 5% monthly invoice) in case of measurable breach during the first 6 months while the runbook is stabilized.

If Sales accepts the price uplift and the customer signs the operational rider, I can route this to Execs for a one-off SLA exception. We should also sync with Legal for the contract language.

Vivek
Director, Platform Reliability
(Attachment: operational_runbook_draft.md)
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Nebula renewal — bespoke uptime & latency asks

Thanks team — good thread. Quick consolidation and next steps:

1) Marissa: outline the commercial offer with committed monthly spend, proposed uplift (we'll start at 35% above hosted baseline) and timeline for the 30-day mirrored staging.
2) Karthik: please draft the technical rider (2–3 pages) that states the model constraints and operational pre-conditions (token caps, no streaming for latency tier, fallback thresholds). Target by EOD tomorrow.
3) Vivek: finalize the runbook and the one-time mitigation credit language. If you can sign off on operational readiness we will take to Legal & Finance for exception approval.
4) I'll raise with Legal & Finance simultaneously — please flag anything in your drafts that would materially change cost or risk.

Assuming the above items align, I am prepared to recommend this for Exec sign-off. Marissa, aim to have the customer accept the commercial terms and start the DocuSign flow by Sept 20 to meet their signature timeline.

Attaching a draft SLA commitment template for review (SLA-commitment-draft.docx). I will put a short note in the exec packet after we have the tech rider and runbook.

Thanks — Ava
VP, Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: SLA-commitment-draft.docx)
